   314	/**
   315	 * Download one file (gguf or mmproj) to `<userData>/local-llm/models/<modelId>/<file>`, streaming its
   316	 * sha256 while writing. Resumable: a `.part` file present from a prior interrupted run is continued via
   317	 * a `Range: bytes=<n>-` request; if the server ignores Range and answers 200 instead of 206, the partial
   318	 * file is discarded and the download restarts clean (never silently corrupts the hash by mixing an
   319	 * un-primed digest with resumed bytes). On a byte-count or checksum mismatch, the partial/finished file
   320	 * is deleted and a typed error is thrown — no corrupt file is ever left at the final path.
   321	 *
   322	 * Exported as the primitive downloadModel() calls per-file — also exercised directly by tests against a
   323	 * local mock HTTP server so checksum-reject/resume/RAM-gate cases never need the real Hugging Face URLs
   324	 * baked into LOCAL_MODELS.
   325	 */
   326	export async function downloadModelFile(
   327	  modelId: string,
   328	  file: 'gguf' | 'mmproj',
   329	  spec: LocalModelFile,
   330	  signal: AbortSignal,
   331	  onProgress?: ProgressCallback
   332	): Promise<void> {
   333	  const dest = filePath(modelId, file)
   334	  mkdirSync(dirname(dest), { recursive: true })
   335	
   336	  if (fileMatches(dest, spec.bytes)) return // already downloaded at the right size
   337	
   338	  const partPath = `${dest}.part`
   339	  let startByte = 0
   340	  if (existsSync(partPath)) {
   341	    const size = statSync(partPath).size
   342	    if (size > 0 && size < spec.bytes) startByte = size
   343	    else safeUnlink(partPath) // stale/oversized .part can't be resumed — start clean
   344	  }
   345	
   346	  // At most one restart: the first pass may discover the server ignored our Range header.
   347	  for (let pass = 0; pass < 2; pass++) {
   348	    const hash = createHash('sha256')
   349	    if (startByte > 0) await hashExistingPart(partPath, hash)
   350	
   351	    const res = await requestRange(spec.url, startByte, signal)
   352	    if (startByte > 0 && res.statusCode !== 206) {
   353	      // Server answered 200 (ignored Range) — the partial bytes can't be trusted as a true prefix of
   354	      // this response body. Discard and restart from zero.
   355	      res.resume()
   356	      safeUnlink(partPath)
   357	      startByte = 0
   358	      continue
   359	    }
   360	
   361	    let received = startByte
   362	    await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
   363	      const out = createWriteStream(partPath, { flags: startByte > 0 ? 'a' : 'w' })
   364	      // IncomingMessage's 'data' event is typed `(chunk: string | Buffer) => void` — we never call
   365	      // res.setEncoding(), so this is always a Buffer at runtime; normalize defensively for the hash.
   366	      res.on('data', (chunk: string | Buffer) => {
   367	        const buf = Buffer.isBuffer(chunk) ? chunk : Buffer.from(chunk)
   368	        hash.update(buf)
   369	        received += buf.length
   370	        onProgress?.({ modelId, file, received, total: spec.bytes })
   371	      })
   372	      res.pipe(out)
   373	      out.on('finish', () => {
   374	        out.close()
   375	        resolve()
   376	      })
   377	      out.on('error', reject)
   378	      res.on('error', reject)
   379	    })
   380	
   381	    const finalSize = statSync(partPath).size
   382	    if (finalSize !== spec.bytes) {
   383	      safeUnlink(partPath)
   384	      throw new IncompleteDownloadError(modelId, file, spec.bytes, finalSize)
   385	    }
   386	    const digest = hash.digest('hex')
   387	    if (digest !== spec.sha256) {
   388	      safeUnlink(partPath)
   389	      localAudit('local.model.checksum_fail', { modelId, file })
   390	      throw new ChecksumMismatchError(modelId, file, spec.sha256, digest)
   391	    }
   392	    renameSync(partPath, dest)
   393	    return
   394	  }
   395	  throw new Error(`Download failed for ${modelId} (${file}): server did not honor the resume request.`)
   396	}

   398	/** Download both files (gguf + mmproj) for a manifest model. Refuses up front if this machine doesn't

   400	export async function downloadModel(id: string, onProgress?: ProgressCallback): Promise<void> {
   401	  const entry = getModel(id)
   402	  assertRamOk(id)
   403	  if (activeDownloads.has(id)) throw new Error(`A download for "${id}" is already in progress.`)

   405	  const controller = new AbortController()
   406	  activeDownloads.set(id, controller)
   407	  try {

   409	    await downloadModelFile(id, 'mmproj', entry.mmproj, controller.signal, onProgress)

   411	  } finally {
   412	    activeDownloads.delete(id)
   413	  }
   414	}

   422	// ─── Cold-start integrity check (F5 hardening) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   423	// isDownloaded()'s byte-size check can't see on-disk corruption (bit rot, a truncated OS-level copy that
   424	// happens to land on the right final size) — verifyIntegrity re-hashes both files against their manifest
   425	// pins once per sidecar spawn (gated by the caller, local.ts's ensureLocalRuntimeStarted, on a cold start
   426	// only) so a corrupt file is caught BEFORE llama-server ever loads it.
   427	
   428	/** Streamed sha256 of a file already fully written to disk — reuses hashExistingPart, the SAME streaming
   429	 *  primitive the download path's own resume-hash priming uses, so there is only one implementation of
   430	 *  "read this file and hash it" in this module. */
   431	async function hashFile(path: string): Promise<string> {
   432	  const hash = createHash('sha256')
   433	  await hashExistingPart(path, hash)

   437	/**
   438	 * Verify one on-disk file against its manifest sha256 pin by re-hashing it fresh off disk. On a mismatch,
   439	 * deletes the corrupt file (mirrors downloadModelFile's own reject+delete behavior — a bad file is never
   440	 * left in place for a later load to trip over) and throws the SAME typed ChecksumMismatchError the
   441	 * download path throws, so callers get one error shape for "this file doesn't match its pin" regardless of
   442	 * when the mismatch was discovered.
   443	 */
   444	async function verifyFileChecksum(modelId: string, file: 'gguf' | 'mmproj', path: string, spec: LocalModelFile): Promise<void> {
   445	  const digest = await hashFile(path)
   446	  if (digest !== spec.sha256) {
   447	    safeUnlink(path)
   448	    localAudit('local.model.checksum_fail', { modelId, file })
   449	    throw new ChecksumMismatchError(modelId, file, spec.sha256, digest)
   450	  }
   451	}

   453	/**

   461	export async function verifyIntegrity(id: string): Promise<void> {

   465	    const path = paths[file]
   466	    if (!existsSync(path)) throw new Error(`Local model "${id}" (${file}) is not downloaded — cannot verify integrity.`)
   467	    await verifyFileChecksum(id, file, path, entry[file])
   468	  }
   469	}

docs/asktoto-architecture.md:258:The combined effect: after `⌘⇧↵`, the overlay shows a skeleton in <50ms, first text in <300ms (network permitting), and a complete useful answer typically in 1.5–3 s for a standard screen question against Claude Sonnet or GPT-4o-mini. The <2 s first-token target is met end-to-end by the prewarm + immediate skeleton + per-RAF flush pipeline; the <2 s useful-answer target is met for fast providers on direct API (Claude, Groq, Fireworks) and degrades gracefully on heavier reasoning tiers with the Thinking… indicator.

docs/asktoto-architecture.md:389:- **Parakeet ASR addon (`sherpa-onnx-node`).** npm's os/cpu-gated `optionalDependencies` only install the `sherpa-onnx-<platform>-<arch>` package matching the machine running `npm install` — cross-building a different target (e.g. `--win` from this macOS dev machine) silently leaves that platform's native addon missing, and `electron-builder`'s `asarUnpack` glob copies whatever happens to be in `node_modules` regardless of target, so the build exits 0 with no native ASR addon for that platform. `scripts/check-sherpa-platform.mjs` hard-fails cross-platform builds unless the target's addon package is present, first attempting a safe, version-pinned auto-provision (`npm install --no-save --force sherpa-onnx-<platform>-<arch>@<sherpa-onnx-node's own installed version>`) before failing closed. It's wired as a gate into every release/installer/dist npm script (`release`, `release:win`, `release:mas`, `installers*`, `dist:local`, `predist:win`).
docs/asktoto-architecture.md:390:- At runtime, `main/parakeet.ts`'s `probeSherpa()` eagerly `require()`s the native addon on the **first** status-or-transcribe call — not lazily, only after a failed transcribe — and memoizes the result (success or failure) forever. This lets Settings show an accurate "Parakeet unavailable" status immediately instead of only after a live call has already failed; `parakeetAddonError()` exposes the last load failure separate from "model not downloaded yet."
docs/asktoto-architecture.md:391:- **FFmpeg import-decoder sidecar.** A reviewed, LGPL-only FFmpeg binary per platform, deliberately untracked in git (`resources/ffmpeg/` is in `.gitignore`) and restored at CI/release time from a GitHub release plus a hash-pinned `manifest.json`. `scripts/check-ffmpeg-sidecar.mjs` verifies the binary's SHA-256 against the manifest and, when the build host's platform matches the target, spawns it to confirm its license banner reads LGPL-only (an `--enable-gpl` build fails the check). `ffmpeg-decoder.ts`'s `bundledFfmpegPath()` returns `null` when the sidecar is absent, so a fresh dev checkout without the binary still runs `npm run dev` fine — only Import Audio's decode step (C.4) is unavailable until the binary is provisioned.
docs/asktoto-architecture.md:403:`intelligence/` is a separate, separately-versioned Vite/React app (`package.json` name `deal-psychology-dashboard`) — not part of the Electron renderer bundle. It ships as its own resizable window (`src/main/intelligence.ts → openIntelligenceWindow()`), loading a static bundle built by `npm run build:intelligence` and packaged into the app via `electron-builder.yml`'s `extraResources` (`intelligence/dist → intelligence`). It talks to the main process through its own minimal preload (`src/preload/intelligence.ts`), exposing only read-only `brain:*` IPC channels, gated by `isIntelligenceSender()` — a document-identity check (window identity *and* the currently-loaded URL matching the bundled document) so a navigation that somehow slipped past the window's `will-navigate` deny still couldn't read the brain. The dashboard mirrors the overlay's Private View behavior: `syncIntelContentProtection()` re-applies `contentProtection` onto the dashboard window whenever the setting flips, since the dashboard aggregates the most sensitive cross-meeting data (people, accounts, deals, quotes, commitments) in one place. If `intelligence/dist` hasn't been built, `bundleIndexHtml()` returns `null` and `openIntelligenceWindow()` fails with a clear "run `npm run build:intelligence`" error — the rest of the app runs fine without it; a developer running only `npm install` + `npm run dev` at the repo root will not have the dashboard's own dependencies installed (`intelligence/` is its own `npm ci`) and won't see it work until that separate build step runs.

docs/asktoto-architecture.md:477:**WebRTC for OpenAI Realtime (future, targeted path).** If true <300 ms partial text transcription is required, add a `useRealtimeTranscription` hook in the renderer that opens a `RTCPeerConnection` to `wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime`, piping the mic `MediaStream` directly. This runs in parallel with (not as a replacement for) the local Whisper/Parakeet pipeline — Realtime gives fast partials, local ASR gives the committed final line (offline-capable, no cost per word). The two paths merge in `commitLine()` with the local decode overwriting the Realtime provisional on a matching timestamp window. Gate the entire path behind `settings.asrEngine='realtime'`.
docs/asktoto-architecture.md:694:4. **New: `systemCache` micro-optimization.** When `contextDocs` changes mid-session (user adds a file), `buildSystem()` is called once and the result is stored in a session-scoped `Map<string, string>` keyed by a 32-bit FNV-1a hash of the inputs. On the next turn, compare hashes and reuse the cached string rather than re-concatenating. Zero network benefit; saves ~0.5ms CPU per turn on large profiles.

docs/asktoto-architecture.md:1178:**In transit**: all LLM providers use HTTPS. CLI providers (`claude-cli`, `codex-cli`) are spawned as local processes — no network. Dust uses HTTPS to `dust.tt` or a configured `dustBaseUrl`. Electron's default CSP blocks non-HTTPS renderer requests.
docs/asktoto-architecture.md:1258:- **Off by default.** `settings.licenseGateEnabled` defaults `false` (`shared/ipc.ts`). While off, `main/license.ts` never makes a network call and no blocking screen renders — the entire subsystem is inert.
docs/asktoto-architecture.md:1260:- **Mechanics.** `main/license.ts`'s `checkLicenseGrace()` is the boot-time verdict function, called via a `license:gate` IPC handler. It implements a soft grace window (7 days — no network call at all while `licenseValid` and inside it) and a hard cap (30 days — even fully offline, a validated license keeps working this long before the app blocks). A 12-hour background interval re-validates via `heartbeat()` whenever the gate is on and the license is currently valid. Each install gets a stable, hostname-independent machine ID (`getMachineId()`, a random UUID persisted to `userData/machine-id.txt`) so a renamed machine or a different OS login doesn't silently burn a new seat.
docs/asktoto-architecture.md:1285:**Portable Windows build has no auto-update, permanently.** `electron-builder.yml` ships a `portable` target (`Metis-Portable-<version>.exe`) alongside the installer, because `electron-updater` has no support for updating a portable EXE (there's no fixed install location to replace — it's just a file the user launched directly). `main/updater.ts → initAutoUpdate()` explicitly bails before any wiring when `process.platform === 'win32' && process.env.PORTABLE_EXECUTABLE_FILE`, logging `'portable build — auto-update unavailable, skipping'`. This is a permanent, by-design carve-out, not a bug: users on the portable build must self-update by re-downloading. See K's Phase 4 checklist for the operational implication.
docs/asktoto-architecture.md:1347:Redis would require a server process, a socket, serialization, and a network hop for data that lives in-process today. Reject it.
docs/asktoto-architecture.md:1395:Métis's store already reads a `managed-settings.json` and merges it with per-user settings. A remote feature flag system is a versioned JSON file hosted on the update CDN (e.g., `https://updates.asktoto.ai/flags/v1.json`), fetched once at startup with a 24h TTL, stored in `userData/remote-flags.json`. The schema: `{ "audioFlushEnabled": true, "parakeetDefault": false, "vectorSearch": false }`. The main process exposes flags via a new `IPC_GET_FLAGS` channel. No SDK dependency, no network call on the hot path, no GDPR concern.
docs/asktoto-architecture.md:1417:Apple Vision (`VNRecognizeTextRequest`) runs on the Neural Engine at ~30–80ms for a full desktop screenshot, entirely on-device, with no tokens spent. Wrapping it as a small Electron native module (`@asktoto/apple-vision`, ~200 lines of Objective-C++ bridged via N-API) lets the main process extract a text layer from the screenshot before the LLM call. The LLM receives: text layer + the image (for UI structure/colour context). Token cost drops by ~60% on text-heavy screens (code editors, document apps). On Windows, skip the OCR step — fall back to image-only (current behaviour). Tesseract.js benchmarks at 600–900ms for a full screenshot on an M-series Mac, which violates the 2.5s first-token budget on screen questions. Reject it. Cloud OCR (Google Vision, AWS Textract) sends the screenshot to a third party and adds 200–600ms network latency — directly opposed to Métis's privacy posture.
docs/asktoto-architecture.md:1433:The risk to manage: `electron-builder` bundles everything in `dependencies` into the app package. Both SDKs together add ~2 MB to the bundle — acceptable. Pin them at minor versions (`"^0.106.0"` → `"~0.106.0"` to block auto-minor bumps that break the streaming format) and audit the changelog before any major upgrade.

Automatic meeting-detection start was shipped, then **removed** — see B.2. The roadmap below is "what to add and harden from here" — not a rebuild.

Product definition\n\n**Positioning (one sentence).** Métis is a permission-based, on-device-first real-time copilot that hears your calls and sees your screen — and hands you a grounded, citable answer in under two seconds — while always showing that it's active and never hiding anything.\n\n**Target users.** People who live inside real-time conversations and screens, where a 10-second pause to \"go look it up\" costs the moment:\n- Client-facing pros — consultants, pre-sales/SE, account managers, customer success, recruiters, founders in pitches.\n- Operators in demos / product reviews / support calls / research sessions who need to read a screen and answer fast.\n- Regulated-industry teams (Mantu's bread and butter — banking, pharma, public sector) who need **on-device transcription + redaction** and can't ship raw audio to a SaaS.\n\n**Top 5 killer use cases.**\n1. **Live meeting/sales copilot** — \"what do I say next?\" → the exact spoken line, grounded in the last 2 minutes + your profile.\n2. **Screen-aware help** — \"what is this showing / draft a reply / explain this error\" → vision answer on the screen you're actually looking at.\n3. **Instant recap + action items** — at any point, \"summarize / who owns what\" → structured, copyable, owner-tagged.\n4. **Answer from YOUR knowledge** — \"what's our standard SLA / find this in our docs\" → Dust-agent retrieval over internal knowledge, cited.\n5. **Recall + resume** — search past meetings, reopen the recap + full transcript, and **resume the session** with the prior context carried forward.\n\n**Why this is meaningfully better than Cluely-style products.**\n- **On-device ASR by default** (Whisper/Parakeet, bundled offline) → lower latency, works on a plane, and the audio never has to leave the machine. If a feature only makes sense for cheating, it doesn't ship.\n\n---\n\n## Section B — UX Design\n\n---\n\n### B.1 First-Run Onboarding & Permissions\n\nMétis's onboarding is a hard gate: `settings.onboardingDone` is `false` → the full App renders nothing but `<Onboarding>` inside a `<Panel>` (`App.tsx`, near the `onboardingDone` check). Don't design around a `detachControls`/`hideToolbar` toggle; neither exists in the current `App.tsx`.\n\n**Quick actions are listening-only, not an idle-state row.** `<QuickActions>` (four ghost-pill shortcuts: What to say next, Fact-check, Explain, Summarize screen) renders only while `showListeningChrome` is true (`listen.listening && view !== 'review' && !stopping`) — i.e. only during an active meeting.     10	## 1. Goal

    12	Add an on-device LLM provider to Métis (Electron 39, TypeScript, mac arm64 + win x64) so
    13	lightweight, latency-critical, privacy-sensitive tasks run locally and free, while heavy
    14	tasks keep using cloud providers:

    17	  `vision` (screenshot understanding/OCR-ish reading) — user-toggleable per task.
    18	- **Cloud (unchanged):** `recap` (post-meeting document), `answer` (brain-grounded Q&A),
    19	  think/deep tiers, brain/graph ingest pipeline (Opus path), follow-up artifacts.
    20	
    21	Success metric (testable): (a) routing unit tests prove that with local enabled+ready for
    22	a task, the FIRST attempt for that task is provider `local` and no cloud attempt happens
    23	when the local stream succeeds; (b) a failover test proves a killed sidecar falls through
    24	to the existing cloud waterfall; (c) `node scripts/prove-local-ttft.mjs` measures suggest
    25	first-token ≤ 1.5 s warm on this M-series Mac against the real sidecar with a 6k-char

   138	### 4.2 Why sidecar (vs node-llama-cpp addon / renderer ONNX)
   139	
   140	1. Vision day-1 via `--mmproj` through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint —
   141	   src/main/llm/openai.ts already sends screenshots as data-URI `image_url`
   142	   (openai.ts:10-17) and already retries without `stream_options` for endpoints that
   143	   reject it (openai.ts:28-33, 110-119). The local strategy is a config shim, not a new
   144	   streaming client.
   145	2. Growing-transcript latency: server-side per-slot prompt caching (cache_prompt,
   146	   default on) + id_slot pinning reuses the transcript-prefix KV across requests — no
   147	   custom KV engineering.
   148	3. Process isolation: a 1-3 GB inference runtime cannot take down the app.
   149	4. Packaging: explicit pinned binaries via fetch script + hard guard = the repo's
   150	   existing ffmpeg-sidecar pattern; avoids the npm optional-natives cross-build trap
   151	   already documented for sherpa-onnx.

   106	/** Download url -> dest with retry+backoff on transient failures (mirrors fetch-models.mjs). A 4xx
   107	 *  (bad pin/URL) never changes on retry, so it breaks out immediately instead of burning the budget.
   108	 *  Skips outright when a non-empty archive already sits at `dest` (fetch-models.mjs's `filePresent`
   109	 *  idiom) — the sha256 check right after this call in provision() is what actually gates trust, so a
   110	 *  leftover archive from an interrupted prior run (e.g. one that failed during extraction, after the
   111	 *  download itself succeeded) is reused instead of re-fetched. */
   112	async function download(url, dest) {
   113	  mkdirSync(dirname(dest), { recursive: true })
   114	  if (existsSync(dest) && statSync(dest).size > 0) {
   115	    console.log(`  [skip-fetch] ${dest.replace(REPO_ROOT, '.')} already on disk`)
   116	    return
   117	  }
   118	  console.log(`  [fetch] ${url}`)
   119	  const part = dest + '.part'
   120	  const MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3
   121	  let lastErr
   122	  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= MAX_ATTEMPTS; attempt++) {
   123	    try {
   124	      const res = await fetchStream(url)
   125	      const total = Number(res.headers['content-length'] || 0)
   126	      let got = 0
   127	      let lastPct = -1
   128	      await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
   129	        const out = createWriteStream(part)
   130	        res.on('data', (chunk) => {
   131	          got += chunk.length
   132	          if (total) {
   133	            const pct = Math.round((got / total) * 100)
   134	            if (pct !== lastPct && pct % 10 === 0) {
   135	              lastPct = pct
   136	              process.stdout.write(`\r    ${pct}%  (${(got / 1024 / 1024).toFixed(1)} MB)`)
   137	            }
   138	          }
   139	        })
   140	        res.pipe(out)
   141	        out.on('finish', () => { process.stdout.write('\n'); out.close(resolve) })
   142	        out.on('error', reject)
   143	        res.on('error', reject)
   144	      })
   145	      const size = statSync(part).size
   146	      if (total && size !== total) throw new Error(`incomplete download: got ${size} of ${total} bytes`)
   147	      renameSync(part, dest)
   148	      return
   149	    } catch (err) {
   150	      lastErr = err
   151	      try { unlinkSync(part) } catch { /* .part may not exist */ }
   152	      const clientErr = /HTTP 4\d\d/.test(err.message || '')
   153	      if (attempt < MAX_ATTEMPTS && !clientErr) {
   154	        const backoffMs = 1000 * 2 ** (attempt - 1)
   155	        console.log(`  [retry ${attempt}/${MAX_ATTEMPTS - 1}] ${err.message}; waiting ${backoffMs}ms`)

   157	      } else break
   158	    }
   159	  }
   160	  throw lastErr
   161	}

   167	/** Locate the directory (searching down from root) that directly contains `filename` — the mac tarball

   170	function findDirContaining(root, filename, depth = 3) {

   172	  if (depth <= 0) return null
   173	  for (const entry of readdirSync(root, { withFileTypes: true })) {
   174	    if (entry.isDirectory()) {

   178	  }

   185	 *  the other example binaries) is intentionally discarded — Métis only ever spawns llama-server. */

   187	  const tmpDir = `${destDir}.extract-tmp`

   192	  if (!sourceDir) throw new Error(`${binaryName} not found anywhere under the extracted archive ${archivePath}.`)

   194	  mkdirSync(destDir, { recursive: true })
   195	  for (const f of readdirSync(sourceDir)) {
   196	    if (f === binaryName || f.endsWith(keepExt)) copyFileSync(join(sourceDir, f), join(destDir, f))

   198	  rmSync(tmpDir, { recursive: true, force: true })

   216	  await download(BASE_URL + asset.file, archivePath)
   217	
   218	  // Verify BEFORE extraction — never unpack an archive we haven't confirmed the integrity of.
   219	  const actual = sha256Of(archivePath)
   220	  if (actual !== asset.sha256) {
   221	    unlinkSync(archivePath)
   222	    throw new Error(`${asset.file} sha256 mismatch: expected ${asset.sha256}, got ${actual}. Deleted; re-run to retry.`)
   223	  }
   224	
   225	  extractRuntime(archivePath, asset.dest, asset.binary, asset.keepExt)
   226	  unlinkSync(archivePath)
   227	
   228	  if (!existsSync(join(asset.dest, asset.binary))) {
   229	    throw new Error(`${asset.binary} missing from ${asset.dest} after extraction — check the archive contents.`)
   230	  }
   231	  writeFileSync(join(asset.dest, '.sha256'), asset.sha256 + '\n')
   232	  console.log(`  [ok] provisioned (${asset.sha256.slice(0, 12)}…)`)
   233	}
   234	
   235	// ─── Main ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   236	const VALID = new Set(['mac', 'win', 'all'])
   237	// No arg: auto-detect the current platform (mirrors check-ffmpeg-sidecar.mjs / check-sherpa-platform.mjs's
   238	// `process.argv[2] || process.platform` fallback) so the bare `npm run fetch:llama` convenience script works.
   239	const target = process.argv[2] || (process.platform === 'win32' ? 'win' : 'mac')
   240	if (!VALID.has(target)) {
   241	  console.error('Usage: node scripts/fetch-llama-server.mjs mac|win|all')
   242	  process.exit(2)
   243	}
   244	
   245	async function main() {
   246	  console.log(`=== fetch-llama-server: provisioning resources/llama/ for target "${target}" (tag ${TAG}) ===`)
   247	  mkdirSync(LLAMA_DIR, { recursive: true })
   248	  for (const key of assetKeysFor(target)) {
   249	    await provision(key, ASSETS[key])
   250	  }
   251	  console.log('\n=== fetch-llama-server complete ===')
   252	}
   253	
   254	main().catch((err) => {
   255	  console.error('\nfetch-llama-server FAILED:', err.message)
   256	  process.exit(1)
   257	})

   336	export const PROVIDER_IDS = Object.keys(PROVIDERS) as ProviderId[]
   337	
   338	/**
   339	 * Auto-detect the provider from a pasted key by its unambiguous prefix.
   340	 * Returns null when the key shape is shared by several providers (bare `sk-…`) so the
   341	 * caller leaves the user's current selection alone instead of guessing wrong.
   342	 * Order matters: sk-ant- and sk-or- must beat a generic sk- guess (which we never make).
   343	 */
   344	export function detectProvider(key: string): ProviderId | null {
   345	  const k = key.trim()
   346	  if (!k) return null
   347	  for (const id of PROVIDER_IDS) {
   348	    const pat = PROVIDERS[id].keyPattern
   349	    if (pat && new RegExp(pat).test(k)) return id
   350	  }
   351	  return null
   352	}
   353	
   354	/**
   355	 * Pull Dust connection bits out of a pasted Dust URL so the user never has to find an id by hand.
   356	 * Handles workspace (`/w/<id>`), region (dust.tt vs eu.dust.tt), and the agent id from a builder
   357	 * link (`/builder/agents/<id>`), an agent link (`/assistant/<id>`), or a `?assistant=<id>` query.
   358	 */
   359	export function parseDustUrl(input: string): {
   360	  workspaceId?: string
   361	  baseUrl?: string
   362	  agentId?: string
   363	} {
   364	  const out: { workspaceId?: string; baseUrl?: string; agentId?: string } = {}
   365	  const raw = input.trim()
   366	  if (!/dust\.tt/i.test(raw)) return out
   367	  try {
   368	    const u = new URL(raw.startsWith('http') ? raw : `https://${raw}`)
   369	    if (/(^|\.)eu\.dust\.tt$/i.test(u.host)) out.baseUrl = 'https://eu.dust.tt'
   370	    else if (/(^|\.)dust\.tt$/i.test(u.host)) out.baseUrl = 'https://dust.tt'
   371	    const w = u.pathname.match(/\/w\/([^/]+)/)
   372	    if (w) out.workspaceId = w[1]
   373	    // Only unambiguous agent-shaped sources may set agentId. A bare /assistant/<id> path segment on
   374	    // dust.tt is a CONVERSATION id, not an agent — treating it as one silently pointed the app's base
   375	    // agent at garbage when a user pasted a chat link. Agent ids appear in the builder path
   376	    // (/builder/agents|assistants/<sId>) or in the ?assistant=/assistantId=/agentId= query params.
   377	    const a = u.pathname.match(/\/builder\/(?:agents|assistants)\/([^/?#]+)/)
   378	    const qa =
   379	      u.searchParams.get('assistant') ||
   380	      u.searchParams.get('assistantId') ||
   381	      u.searchParams.get('agentId')
   382	    if (a && a[1] && a[1] !== 'new') out.agentId = a[1]
   383	    else if (qa) out.agentId = qa
   384	  } catch {
   385	    /* not a URL — leave empty */
   386	  }
   387	  return out
   388	}

   394	): string {
   395	  const def = PROVIDERS[id]

   401	export type ModelTier = 'base' | 'think' | 'deep'
   402	
   403	/**
   404	 * Resolve the model/agent for a routing tier.
   405	 *  - base  → the user's chosen base model, else the provider's fast/cheap model (e.g. Haiku).
   406	 *  - think → the user's chosen thinking model, else the provider's reasoning model (e.g. Sonnet),
   407	 *            else falls back to the base/default so a provider without a distinct think model still works.
   408	 *  - deep  → the user's chosen deep model, else the provider's deepest model (e.g. Opus), else the
   409	 *            think model, so a provider without a distinct deep model degrades to its reasoning model.
   410	 * For Dust the "model" is an agent sId: base/think/deep = providerModels.dust / thinkModels.dust / deepModels.dust.
   411	 */
   412	export function resolveModelTier(
   413	  id: ProviderId,
   414	  providerModels: Partial<Record<string, string>>,
   415	  thinkModels: Partial<Record<string, string>>,
   416	  tier: ModelTier,
   417	  deepModels: Partial<Record<string, string>> = {}
   418	): string {
   419	  const def = PROVIDERS[id]
   420	  const base = (providerModels[id] || '').trim()
   421	  const think = (thinkModels[id] || '').trim() || def.thinkModel || ''
   422	  if (tier === 'deep') {
   423	    const deep = (deepModels[id] || '').trim()
   424	    return deep || def.deepModel || think || base || def.defaultModel || ''
   425	  }
   426	  if (tier === 'think') {
   427	    return think || base || def.defaultModel || ''
   428	  }
   429	  return base || def.fastModel || def.defaultModel || ''
   430	}

   432	/** Cost/safety guardrail (per Tony): the CLI provider only ever answers as Sonnet in the interactive
   433	 *  ask flow, never Haiku, never Opus, regardless of routeTier's escalation (hard/coding questions,
   434	 *  factcheck, or thinkingMode 'always' would otherwise reach Opus here). The direct Anthropic API
   435	 *  key's base/think tiers are pinned to Haiku/Sonnet so a stray providerModels edit can't drift them.
   436	 *  Deep tier is deliberately EXEMPT on both: that's the Graph extraction pipeline's reserved path to
   437	 *  Opus (brain/ingest.ts and graphify.ts call resolveModelTier directly and never reach this function). */
   438	export function applyInteractiveGuardrail(id: ProviderId, tier: ModelTier, model: string): string {
   439	  if (id === 'claude-cli') return PROVIDERS['claude-cli'].thinkModel ?? 'sonnet'
   440	  if (id === 'anthropic' && tier === 'base') return PROVIDERS.anthropic.fastModel
   441	  if (id === 'anthropic' && tier === 'think') return PROVIDERS.anthropic.thinkModel ?? model
   442	  return model
   443	}

   445	/** Is Dust configured with valid credentials right now — independent of whether it's the globally active
   446	 *  `provider`. Used to decide whether a specific task (recap, follow-up email, Spotlight Ref) can cascade
   447	 *  into Dust even while another provider (e.g. Kimi) handles everyday Q&A. */
   448	export function isDustReady(
   449	  hasKeys: Partial<Record<string, boolean>>,
   450	  dustWorkspaceId: string,
   451	  providerModels: Partial<Record<string, string>>
   452	): boolean {
   453	  return !!hasKeys['dust'] && !!dustWorkspaceId.trim() && !!providerModels['dust']
   454	}

   456	/**
   457	 * Whether a Dust agent's underlying model can read images (screenshots). Dust messages are text-only, so
   458	 * a screenshot is uploaded as a file the AGENT'S model then interprets — which only helps if that model
   459	 * is multimodal. Unlike a provider's static `vision` flag this is per-agent, derived from the model Dust
   460	 * reports (`modelProviderId` + `modelId` — the same signal the agent picker uses). It errs toward the
   461	 * families whose *current* models are multimodal; a rare misclassification degrades gracefully (a
   462	 * text-only agent gets a best-effort answer, or a vision agent is skipped for another vision provider).
   463	 */
   464	export function dustAgentVision(
   465	  agent: { modelProviderId?: string; modelId?: string } | null | undefined
   466	): boolean {
   467	  if (!agent) return false
   468	  const provider = (agent.modelProviderId || '').toLowerCase()
   469	  const model = (agent.modelId || '').toLowerCase()
   470	  // Explicit multimodal hints in the model id win regardless of provider (qwen-vl, pixtral, *-vision).
   471	  if (/vision|pixtral|(^|[^a-z])vl([^a-z]|$)/.test(model)) return true
   472	  switch (provider) {
   473	    case 'anthropic':
   474	      // Every Claude model Dust exposes (Claude 3 and newer) accepts images.
   475	      return true
   476	    case 'openai':

Commit:     Tony Walteur <tony.walteur@gmail.com>
CommitDate: Sat Jul 11 07:58:08 2026 -0400

    Fix model-switch races found by ship-audit round 3
    
    A superseded sidecar's exit handler could clobber the replacement
    instance's ownership (orphaning it at quit and firing a spurious
    crash/auto-restart) — the handler is now generation-guarded by process
    identity. Switching models while the old sidecar was running also
    skipped the cold-start sha256 re-verification — integrity is now
    re-verified whenever the target model differs from the active one.
    Prewarm docs/tests now state the history-parity limitation honestly:
    full prefix parity covers the history-free suggest path; turns carrying
    copilot history still share the system-block prefix, and delta prefill
    keeps TTFT inside budget even on a full miss.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

+describe('G1 — exit handler generation guard', () => {
+  it('a stale exit event from the OLD sidecar, arriving AFTER a switch to a NEW one is already healthy, does not clobber the new instance, fire a crash audit, or trigger an auto-restart — and will-quit-style stop() still kills the NEW instance', async () => {
+    const pathsA = { gguf: '/m/a.gguf', mmproj: '/m/a.mmproj' }
+    const pathsB = { gguf: '/m/b.gguf', mmproj: '/m/b.mmproj' }
+
+    const p1 = start(pathsA, 'mac')
+    emitListening(0, 55501)
+    await p1
+    const procA = spawnState.procs[0]
+
+    // Reproduce the real-world race deterministically: the OS-level 'exit' event for a SIGKILL'd process
+    // can land on a LATER tick than the kill() call itself. Override the mock's auto-fire-on-kill so we
+    // control exactly WHEN A's exit event arrives — specifically, after B is already confirmed healthy —
+    // instead of relying on however fast the queued microtask from kill() happens to resolve.
+    procA.kill = vi.fn(() => {
+      procA.killed = true
+    })
+
+    const p2 = start(pathsB, 'mac')
+    await waitUntil(() => spawnState.calls.length === 2)
+    emitListening(1, 55502)
+    await p2
+    expect(isRunning()).toBe(true)
+    expect(baseURL()).toBe('http://127.0.0.1:55502/v1')
+
+    // A's exit event finally arrives, well after the switch to B completed and B is healthy/running.

+    await Promise.resolve()
+    await Promise.resolve()

+    expect(spawnState.calls.length).toBe(2) // no auto-restart spawn triggered by the stale exit

+    // because A's stale exit nulled the module's `child` reference out from under it.
